title: Parker's breakdown begins; 'The Gypsy' and 'Idaho'
summary: Parker's nerves collapsed at the Finale Club, yet he played unforgettable moments on 'The Gypsy' and 'Idaho'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, we had some great times. In fact, this is where Charlie Parker started his nervous breakdown, when he had his nervous breakdown....

During this time we were at the Finale Club. He was trying to solve his problem without any medical attention, and he had lost complete control of his nerves. You know, his neck would turn around, his arms would fly out, he'd walk a step, run a step -- his nervous system was completely wrecked, you know. I was sitting watching him, and he never complained about his condition, and it was getting progressively worse.

And one thing I'll always remember, a lady came up to the bandstand and asked the band to play "The Gypsy." Do you remember the tune "The Gypsy"? And "The Gypsy" had just come out. Nobody had heard "The Gypsy." So Howard says, "Anybody know 'The Gypsy'?" And he says, "Yeah." And so he

played "The Gypsy," and it was classic, you know. That's the reason they recorded it later, during his breakdown, because he remembered him playing... Ross Russell remembered this performance he did on "The Gypsy."

Also, something else that was really fantastic. I really heard this whole thing come to a head in a solo that he played on the tune "Idaho." He played something on his instrument that everybody in the place sighed at the same time. You could hear it, you know, everybody said [SHARP GASP] And most of the people in there didn't know who he was, you know, during that time. But he struck everybody in this place, you know.
